newsitem.title: SPAIN: Christmas Eve eyed as Spain key rate cut day.
newsitem.headline: Christmas Eve eyed as Spain key rate cut day.

text.p: Spanish economists are starting to eye December 24 as the day on which a cut in Spain's key money market rate is likely to emerge, although they were not ruling out a cut on December 13 either.

"We think both dates are highly likely to produce a rate cut, but against a cut on the thirteenth is the fact that the Bank of Spain won't formally know the November inflation figure," said Antonio Zamora, economist at Analistas Financieros Internacionales (AFI).
The Consumer Price Index (CPI) is also due for release on November 13, but the Bank of Spain's repurchase (repo) auction results are usually announced earlier in the morning.
The central bank has cut its key money rate, the repo, six times this year to 6.75 percent. At its last regular tender, on Tuesday, the central bank left rates unchanged as expected.
"From a formal point of view it would be more elegant to cut on the twenty-fourth," according to Xavier Segura, head of research at Caja Catalunya.
However if the Bank of Spain were to cut rates on December 13 it would hardly surprise a market which is "crying out for it," according to AFI's Zamora.
Some analysts pointed out that there have been occasions where the monetary authorities have cut rates before the CPI has been released, and for that reason the 13th will be the day.
"The Bank of Spain likes to move ahead. There's been more than one occasion when it's cut rate before inflation has been released," said Carmen Alcaide at Banco Bilbao Vizcaya research.
She said there were three reasons backing a cut in rates at the next repo: "good inflation performance, a strong peseta and the flattening of the (bond) yield curve."
However others saw no reason for the central bank to rush.
"I don't see any reason to hurry because the Bundesbank won't raise rates for a few months and neither is there any urgency from the point of view of exchange rates," AFI's Zamora said.
Other analysts were not ruling out a delay until next year.
"What's the significance of a rate cut this year for the Bank of Spain if it's true that technically it has room to cut any time?" said a research director at a private Spanish bank.

"Of course meeting inflation targets is the main aim and with that in mind if I had to choose I'd say December 24 will be the day. Also from a formal point of view, the twenty-fourth's the day," he added.
The main thing the authorities will be watching is the inflation performance at the start of 1997, key for Spain's inclusion in Europe's single currency, analysts said.
Analysts were less doubtful as to how much the central bank will lop off its money market rate, with most expecting a 50 basis point move.
"I think the Bank of Spain is thinking of half a point with a solid argument rather than a quarter point with doubts (attached)," said the research head.
